document_title: Two Land Rights Decided. One Still Open.
post_copy:
"It's hard to look at that and not call this rushed," Sen. Cathy Giessel said of DNR's Alaska LNG lease decision.

UPDATE. DNR approved a 50-year North Slope data center lease and decided to convey about 6,800 acres near Houston to AIDEA. The third is Alaska LNG's 800-mile gas line. Its comments close at 5:00 p.m. November 25th.

DNR proposes converting the line's two conditional leases into full leases. Per DNR, that is not a permit to build. Seven conditions stay as later gates.

Hearings run virtually November 23rd and in Anchorage November 24th. A decision could come before the December 7th handoff.

The three files, the hearing in quotes, the seven conditions, Houston at true scale and every window on one calendar are all here.

If conversion is not a permit to build, what do investors gain from having it before December 7th?

#AlaskaLNG #AlaskaDNR #AlaskaLand

slides.headline: Two land rights decided. One still open.
Two are pressed. One is still a circle.
slides.body: DNR approved a 50-year North Slope data center lease and, on November 10th, published its decision conveying about 6,800 acres near Houston to AIDEA. Its proposed decision on Alaska LNG's 800-mile corridor still takes comment.

slides.kicker: JOINT HOUSE AND SENATE RESOURCES MEETING
slides.headline: "It's hard to look at that and not call this rushed."
slides.body: DNR is "doing our best to advance (the decision) as expeditiously as we can."

slides.headline: A full lease is not a permit to build.
slides.body: DNR proposes turning the line's conditional leases into full ones. Its own text says conversion "does not grant AGDC permission to start construction," and every condition stays a gate at a later step.

slides.headline: Part of the case is in a sealed envelope.
slides.body: DNR cites planned capitalization of more than $50 billion and letters of intent for more than 60 percent of capacity, which it calls non-binding. The Department of Revenue's economics analysis is confidential. Per ADN, Crowther acknowledged departing from DNR's normal process.

slides.headline: Little Troublesome Creek Campground. One of the existing uses the gas line lease must still address.
6,800 acres to AIDEA. The borough wants it elsewhere.
slides.body: DNR's decision conveys about 6,800 acres, down from almost 20,000 first proposed. On November 13th the Mat-Su Borough asked DNR to reconsider and named Point MacKenzie.

slides.headline: Both decided over heavy opposition.
slides.body: North Slope, a 50-year lease on about 715 acres for a 1 to 3 gigawatt data center, drew more than 1,200 responses, most opposed. Houston drew more than 2,300 comments, almost all opposed. Each decision now has a reconsideration window.

editor_notes_for_email: This story updates No.111 (Houston, ADL 234762) and No.112 (STAK, ADL 422741) and adds the Alaska LNG lease conversion (ADL 421296 and ADL 421297), which no earlier deck covered. The two scanned primaries, DNR's 17-page proposed decision and the Mat-Su Borough's two-page letter, have no text layer, so the showrunner read them as page images. No fetched page links the gas line to data centers, so the deck never makes that link and treats the three files as one department's decisions on one calendar. Effort ran at medium for this run even though .claude/settings.json carries high.
